description: KarnÃ¶ffel is the oldest identifiable European card game, dating back to 1426. It is a trick-taking game with a unique 'chosen suit' mechanism where certain cards have special powers. The game is historically significant as the ancestor of many modern card games including the trump mechanism.

history.origins: KarnÃ¶ffel is the oldest identifiable European card game, first mentioned in a town ordinance of NÃ¶rdlingen, Bavaria in 1426. The name likely derives from the German 'Karnickel' (rabbit) or refers to the Under (Jack) card. The game represents a crucial step in the evolution of card games, introducing the concept of a 'chosen suit' with special powers.

history.cultural: KarnÃ¶ffel holds immense historical significance in card game history. It was mentioned in medieval literature and church sermons (often disapprovingly). The game is now primarily of interest to historians and collectors, though it is still played by some traditional game enthusiasts.
history.evolution: KarnÃ¶ffel was revolutionary for its time, introducing a suit with special powers that could beat cards of other suits regardless of rank. This concept evolved into the modern trump suit mechanism. The game influenced the development of Tarot, Triumph, and ultimately modern trick-taking games.

rules.objective: Win tricks by playing higher cards or using the special powers of the KarnÃ¶ffel suit cards. Score points based on cards captured.
rules.gameplay:
1. Deal 12 cards to each player
2. Determine the KarnÃ¶ffel (chosen) suit
3. The KarnÃ¶ffel suit has special powers:
   - KarnÃ¶ffel (Under/Jack of KarnÃ¶ffel): Beats all cards except the higher KarnÃ¶ffel cards
   - Higher cards in KarnÃ¶ffel suit also have special ranks
4. Non-KarnÃ¶ffel cards rank normally within their suits
5. Players must follow suit if possible
6. If unable to follow, can play any card
7. The highest card of the led suit wins, unless a KarnÃ¶ffel card is played
8. KarnÃ¶ffel cards can win tricks even when not following suit
9. Trick winner leads to next trick
10. Score based on cards captured
